displayedOptions.name: Fault Atlas
displayedOptions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one realistic, production-quality website visual direction named "Fault Atlas" for FlakeMap, a research-stage agent reliability lab. Output a single continuous 1440px-wide, approximately 2400px-tall scrollable marketing webpage design showing three consecutive chapters of ONE coherent direction, not a montage of alternatives. Each chapter has a focused primary message, generous space, clear hierarchy and readable UI. No browser or device frame. Current date anchor 8 October 2026.
The four attached screenshots are inspiration ONLY: first Blackbird Stories for expressive bold typography and careful letter spacing; second Blackbird menu for confident scale and editorial layout; third and fourth Noomo for the continuity of one subject across fullscreen narrative transitions. Do not reproduce their logos, wording, bird, feathers, photography, or layouts.
Brand direction: warm porcelain white, carbon-black typography, sharply controlled burnt-orange diagnostic accent, occasional pale apricot chapter surface. Authored editorial art direction and a visually memorable workflow map, with minimal generic SaaS styling. Two type families maximum: carefully kerned substantial grotesk sans for headings and UI, contrasting elegant italic editorial serif for one or two emphasized words. Bold letterforms must have optical breathing room, refined proportions, intentional tracking and no awkwardly enormous clumsy blocks. Body/UI 14–16px equivalent at 1440 width. No rainbow gradients, glossy orbs, robots, stars, neon blue, fake logos or customer quotes.
Chapter one, roughly 850px: clean full-width header on porcelain, original provisional FlakeMap wordmark with tiny branch-shaped emblem, nav Products / Platform / Pricing, small "Concept preview", orange primary button "Request a replay study". Asymmetric editorial hero, large left headline exactly "Find the step.\nExplain the failure." The word failure can be tasteful italic serif. Short description "Controlled replay for multi-step agent workflows." Two buttons "Explore the demo" and "How it works". Right/bottom signature scene: a spacious three-dimensional architectural field of thin dark paths and small porcelain tool tiles, actually a readable order lookup → stock check → PO draft path; a burnt-orange retry loop visibly splits into two final draft artifacts. The same thin path extends into subsequent chapter. Keep this visual an integrated part of the whole white page, no framed hero illustration. Small label "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA".
Chapter two, roughly 730px: full-width apricot canvas, giant quiet background word "DIVERGENCE" partially behind the original connected-path graphic. Main copy "The same workflow.\nA different outcome." Left baseline path continues once. Right candidate path branches at a clearly labeled "Stock API timeout", retry and late response both reach two separate draft objects labeled PO-204-A / PO-204-B. A horizontal editorial row of three compact evidence slips shows "01 / Tool condition", "02 / Failing transition", "03 / Duplicate artifact". This should suggest a section that becomes a horizontal scroll scene, but show a stable readable captured state. Subtle chapter indicator 02 / 05; short typography-based hint "Scroll to inspect". No instructional arrows layered onto the screenshot.
Chapter three, roughly 820px: return to porcelain, headline "Evidence for the next release." Precise high-quality product view integrated in the page rather than app-card nesting. Visible DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA and CONCEPT PREVIEW ribbon. Workspace "PO-204 / Purchase-order approval", tabs Replay / Run matrix / Review. Controls Baseline v0.8 / Candidate v0.9, Fault: Timeout, Seed: 104. Side-by-side fine-line timelines and opened evidence panel: "Expected: 1 draft", "Observed: 2 drafts", "Failed transition: stock check → PO draft". Reviewer local mock state "Needs review" and "Annotate simulated failure", secondary "Export mock report". One minimal run condition table with no opaque global quality score. Clearly stamp metrics "Simulation only". No live model scoring, connected services, real writes or real customer claims. Small footer carries "FlakeMap — Agent Reliability Lab" and "Concept preview".
All content must fit cleanly with strong spacing, baseline alignment, subtle borders, restrained rounding, and typography craftsmanship. It should feel like a senior studio's original premium SaaS identity. These are static visual concept mockups, not real product screenshots. Focus on the main replay workflow; don't add a full feature inventory. Show the three chapters as a cohesive long page with contrasting composition and continuity.

displayedOptions.name: Prism Replay
displayedOptions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a single independent realistic premium website visual direction named "Prism Replay" for FlakeMap, a research-stage agent reliability lab. One continuous 1440px-wide, about 2400px-tall scrollable webpage showing THREE consecutive scenes of ONE design, no collage of alternatives, no browser/device chrome. Current date anchor 8 October 2026. Production-quality spacing, typography, fine details and sharp readable UI.
Actual attached references: first two are Blackbird bold typographic identity/menu; last two are Noomo's cinematic feather/bird chapters. Borrow Noomo's seamless full-screen narrative continuity, atmospheric depth, fine serif/sans contrast and a persistent subject moving across the page. Borrow Blackbird's confidence and careful kerning. Create original FlakeMap artwork; no birds, feathers, borrowed logos, customer portraits, brand assets or copied layouts.
This direction should be visibly distinct from a geometric tile diagram: a light immersive spatial story built around one translucent folded TRACE RIBBON, an elegant physically plausible continuous thin sheet that represents the PO workflow. Subtle engraved step tickmarks on it; the strip splits at a fault seam into two destination paths. A meaningful topological route, not a random glowing loop. Pearl, fog-white, pale ice/sage interference tint, dark midnight slate text, selective deep plum fault annotation. Tiny warm copper mark for the exact seam. No glossy orb, robot, generic neural nodes, heavy purple gradients, neon, fake customers or compliance marks. Overall mostly LIGHT. Airy cinematic material depth comes from one custom iridescent route object, not a whole busy science fiction background. Two typefaces: beautifully tracked contemporary sans and dramatic but legible editorial italic serif. UI body 14–16px equivalent. Strong dark text contrast even over pale material.
First scene 900px: fine elegant horizontal nav; left original provisional FlakeMap wordmark with small route-fold symbol; Products, Platform, Pricing; right "Concept preview" and small dark button "Request a replay study". Big readable central/left editorial headline exactly "Every path has\na breaking point." Use italic serif for "breaking point." with calm negative space. Copy: "Explore the step where an agent workflow changes." Two distinct CTAs "Explore the demo" and "See the workflow". Behind/below typography, one large luminous translucent trace ribbon moves gently from far left toward right with engraved labels Order lookup, Stock check, PO draft, and an understated fault-seam marker. Integrated in the environment, never inside an illustration rectangle. Delicate horizontal plane shadow gives it weight. Persistent small badge "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA". Small bottom chapter strip: "01 / FOLLOW THE WORKFLOW" and "Scroll to replay". The imagined pointer interaction refracts the route surface subtly; no cursor effects need to be painted into this static image.
Second scene 720px: seamlessly continue the same pearl world, scene zooms into the seam and ribbon forks across the viewport. Text is asymmetrically right-aligned in the composition, not centred again: "A timeout.\nA retry.\nTwo drafts." Use one oversize faint background word "REPLAY" and precise slim annotation lines. Label seam "Injected stock timeout", upper path "Retry completes", lower path "Late response completes"; two subtle document evidence objects PO-204-A / PO-204-B. No magical duplication; label "Both paths reach PO draft". Left narrow chapter count 02 / 05. Under it a clean horizontal progress rail with tool events and a small right text block "Acceptance criterion / Exactly one draft per order". This is the staged cinematic scroll moment with sequential words appearing in place, not generic cards.
Third scene 780px: the ribbon fades into a precise white product inspection area—an immersive story becomes an actual usable-looking workbench. Full width heading "Now inspect the evidence." A clean readable synthetic app screen with compact product masthead "FlakeMap / PO-204", persistent DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA and CONCEPT PREVIEW. Horizontal controls baseline v0.8 / candidate v0.9 / fault Timeout / seed 104. Main evidence-first layout: left broad vertical candidate trace with timestamps on 8 Oct 2026, timeout → retry succeeds → PO-204-A → late response → PO-204-B; right opened artifact comparison with "Expected 1 draft" / "Observed 2 drafts". Bottom restrained reviewer bar "Rubric: exactly one draft" / "Needs review" / "Annotate simulated failure", secondary "Export mock report". Stamp "Simulation only" beside every metric. Do not invent live services or real AI model execution. Avoid excessive tabs, controls or feature inventory. A fine-line baseline small reference row shows one artifact only. This frame feels dense enough to be credible but generous enough to read. Footer carries concept status.
The image is a static art-direction mockup, never an actual deployed site screenshot. Three consecutive scenes should suggest a continuous scroll film whose original single ribbon evolves from workflow to divergence to reviewed evidence. High-end visual authorship, refined intentional typography and premium product credibility.

displayedOptions.name: Release Edition
displayedOptions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one independent production-quality visual direction named "Release Edition" for FlakeMap, the proposed agent reliability lab. Output ONE coherent long marketing website, 1440px wide approximately 2400px tall, with three consecutive scroll chapters. No browser chrome, no devices, no multiple alternative concepts in the same image. Current date anchor is 8 October 2026. This is a static concept mockup.
The four attached user screenshots are references only. Blackbird's Stories and menu demonstrate substantial bold fonts with beautifully tuned letter spacing, black outlines, asymmetrical editorial grouping and sophisticated scale. Noomo demonstrates choreographed scene changes and words entering in place. Borrow these principles, not any logos, assets, words, palettes, layouts or imagery. This direction must be original and visibly different from spatial 3D tile or translucent ribbon compositions.
Brand: an authored typographic engineering journal. Chalk white and true black, a deliberate muted chartreuse/citron chapter canvas, small aubergine fault accents. Flat editorial graphic design, print-like rules, tiny technical captions, sharp rectangular geometry with selective large radius cards. No glassmorphism, gradients, 3D islands, organic swooshes, robot/orb, stock photography, particle wallpaper or generic features grid. Two typography families maximum: strong rounded contemporary grotesk with exact kerning for display and UI, contrasting refined italic serif for short narrative accents. Typography should be aesthetic and premium even when very bold, with roomy margins and tuned letter spacing. Body 14–16px equivalent. Show excellent alignment and deliberate button, arrow, border and footer craft.
Chapter one approximately 850px, on white: horizontal header with a distinctive original provisional FlakeMap wordmark in heavy grotesk at left, tiny "Agent Reliability Lab" below, spacious Products / Platform / Pricing nav, black outlined pill "Request a replay study" at right and clear "Concept preview". Bold central headline exactly "One workflow.\nMany ways to fail." in two large well-spaced balanced lines; italic serif only for "to fail." Supporting text "Find the failing transition. Review the evidence. Define the next release gate." Two CTAs primary black pill "Explore the synthetic demo", secondary text arrow "How replay works". Behind/below headline a huge pale grey background word "REPLAY", and an overlapping editorial strip of THREE realistic flat evidence sheets positioned with careful composition, not random tilted cards. One is "PO-204 / Baseline", one is "Stock API / Timeout", one is "Candidate / Duplicate draft"; each contains a miniature readable portion of actual product UI, trace rows or artifact IDs. Edges have confident slim black borders, no fake images. Integrated hero shows tangible evidence before features. Persistent "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA".
Chapter two approximately 730px: FULL-WIDTH muted citron chapter environment with enormous black background word "WHAT CHANGED?" cropped only as a deliberate decorative heading, while main explanatory text is fully visible. Left small "02 / INVESTIGATE", narrow chapter title "Follow the failure, step by step." Below, a horizontally arranged narrative track of three large distinct editorial evidence panels and the beginning of a fourth subtly clipped at the far right to suggest horizontal progression: "01 / Inject a timeout" shows stock event, "02 / Watch the retry" shows retry/late-response branching, "03 / Compare the artifacts" shows PO-204-A and PO-204-B, "04 / Review the decision" begins at the right edge. Each panel has its own distinct composition and product fragment, not four identical feature cards. Fine black connector rail unites them. Clear selected-step indicator and left/right buttons. Brief caption "Vertical scroll advances the replay" communicates intended choreography. UI states remain readable and text uses generous rhythm. Original workflow semantics: timeout → retry completes and creates one draft → original late response creates second draft because no shared deduplication guard. Keep synthetic/demo tag visible.
Chapter three approximately 820px: charcoal-black full-width field, heading in cream "A release decision\nwith its evidence." Use elegant serif for "evidence." One large sharp cream workbench surface underneath with restrained rounding. This is the real-looking main product concept, not a generic dashboard. Header "FlakeMap / PO-204" plus persistent DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA and CONCEPT PREVIEW. A compact horizontal toolbar shows Baseline v0.8, Candidate v0.9, Fault: Timeout, Seed:104. Focus on review and matrix: left thin-separated table columns Run / Seed / Condition / Baseline / Candidate, exactly three illustrative rows: R-101 / 101 / Normal / Pass / Pass; R-102 / 102 / Timeout / Pass / Duplicate draft; R-103 / 103 / Delayed response / Pass / Needs review. Do not add aggregates since these three mixed statuses are just illustrative. Right opened evidence drawer title "R-102 / Failed transition", expected 1 draft, observed 2 drafts, source PO-204-A and PO-204-B, rubric "Exactly one draft per order". Bottom human reviewer strip "Needs review" and one dark button "Annotate simulated failure", secondary "Export mock gate report". Clearly "Simulation only; no production reliability estimate". The product review experience is the primary story conclusion, with no real writes or live integration implication. Clean black footer with cream FlakeMap wordmark and Privacy / Contact / Concept preview.
Avoid adding fictitious endorsements, activity notifications, company metrics, live services, SDK endpoints or a feature inventory. Preserve one focused agent replay use case. Every scene has different composition and environment but one consistent visual brand. User wants thoughtfully spaced bold fonts, oversized background typography, editorial cards, vertical-to-horizontal scene changes and a complete premium SaaS feeling. Convey all of those as a refined original designed website concept.
